newsitem.title: USA: Nebraska governor details tax cut plan.
newsitem.headline: Nebraska governor details tax cut plan.

text.p: Nebraska Gov. Ben Nelson detailed plans to cut income and property taxes.
Nelson called for an across-the-board six percent income tax cut, as well as a $160 income tax credit for homeowners.
Karl Bieber, Nelson's spokesman, said the governor would release cost figures for the cuts Wednesday in his state of the state and budget message.
He added that the cuts would be funded through a projected $150 million to $200 million budget surplus for fiscal 1997, which ends June 30.
Nelson also said he would support a one-year study of a local option property tax relief measure. The measure would allow voters to approve a local income tax to fund property tax relief.
